components.title: The port today
components.description: An operating port is a chain of hand-offs. Follow one illustrative container between vessel, quay and yard. PSA reported 14 operating berths on 6 August 2026; this is a dated reference, not a live count.

components.title: Why move west?
components.description: Consolidating container terminals creates a connected port district and releases waterfront land. The finger-pier concept makes efficient use of land and sea space. Open the map context to see Tuas alongside Pasir Panjang and the city terminals.

components.title: Prepare what lies beneath
components.description: Where needed, soft ground was replaced with compacted sand. A prepared rock mound supports the caisson. TEMAROCK combined rock placement, compaction and underwater survey. This exposed profile is representative; actual ground conditions vary.

components.title: Make the giant
components.description: MPA describes a Phase 1 caisson envelope of about 40 × 28 × 28 metres and 15,000 tonnes. Sheltered slip-form production and automated reinforcement handling supported fabrication. Inspect simplified cells and move the formwork; cell layout and reinforcement here are illustrative.

components.title: Float. Place. Retain.
components.description: The caisson was fabricated nearby, towed and submerged onto a prepared foundation. Scrub this movement, then reveal how the wall retains fill and supports the waterfront. The animation explains the relationship, not a ballast, mooring or stability procedure.

components.title: Turn fill into a platform
components.description: More than half of Phase 1 fill came from reused dredged and excavated material. Preloading and drains expedited consolidation. Reveal drains and qualitative water escape, then remove the temporary surcharge. Monitoring checks ground response; animated settlement is exaggerated and has no time scale.

components.title: Connect the working terminal
components.description: Ground stability supports automated operation. Electric AGVs link quay and yard; automated yard equipment is remotely managed. Follow a schematic container hand-off. Reclamation completion and terminal readiness are separate milestones, not one construction completion date.

components.title: Build for decades
components.description: Phase 1 platform elevation is reported as five metres above mean sea level, not above every tide. Environmental assessment and monitoring accompanied reclamation. Compare Phase 2 methods separately; capacity and net-zero milestones are future targets, not achieved conditions.

stages.title: Before the quay
stages.body: Sea and seabed context. No surveyed bathymetry.

stages.title: Seabed preparation
stages.body: Local replacement where needed, followed by a prepared rock mound.

stages.title: Caisson fabrication
stages.body: Representative sheltered fabrication bay, cells and slipform.

stages.title: Tow
stages.body: A floating caisson and tug explain the marine transfer. No verified draft or tow procedure.

stages.title: Placement
stages.body: Seat the caisson on the prepared foundation.

stages.title: Reclamation fill
stages.body: Retain and reuse suitable material behind the quay.

stages.title: Ground improvement
stages.body: Temporary surcharge, drains and monitoring; qualitative relationships.

stages.title: Terminal works
stages.body: Deck, cranes and yard infrastructure follow civil preparation.

stages.title: Operational reference
stages.body: Ship, AGV and yard hand-offs. A schematic cycle, not real dispatch logic.
